overall: Atlanta has had a notably cooler-than-model-expected day, with the running maximum plateauing at 84.2°F since 15:00 ET and no new highs recorded in the past two hours. As of 17:00 ET the temperature has dropped sharply to 75.2°F — nearly 9°F below the day's peak — cooling at a brisk -7.2°F/hr, indicating the afternoon heating cycle is definitively over. The high dewpoint of 71.6°F suggests boundary layer moisture may have suppressed peak heating or convective cloud cover limited solar insolation during peak hours.
forecast_obs_notes: Models showed significant disagreement and all three overshot the observed max: GFS was wildly bullish at 92.0°F, ECMWF at 87.6°F, and NBM at 83.4°F — the NBM came closest but still ran slightly warm relative to the observed 84.2°F plateau. The ensemble signals (89–91°F range) also overestimated, and with the day's heating clearly exhausted, the observed max has decisively undercut all major guidance.
max_temp_prediction: The daily high is almost certainly already locked in at 84.2°F. At 17:00 ET with a cooling rate of -7.2°F/hr and current temp already 9°F below the running max, there is no credible pathway for temperatures to rebound and set a new high this late in the day in Atlanta in early June. Confidence is very high (>95%) that 84.2°F is the final TMAX.
